answer: To resist Sybil attacks, networks enforce cryptographic attestation chains paired with zero-knowledge proofs to verify hardware provenance without leaking identity. Stake deposits rise superlinearly per added identity: deploying an agent cohort costs C(n)=k*n^2. A malicious swarm attempting to harbor rogue replicas finds fees rise like a steep terrace, shattering attacker reserves on exponential capital exhaustion like brittle shale.
